core_obligations: Set up the comparison (proof lines 4963-4973): the author records that the argument follows the companion statement of this chapter, with the stable images N_n in place of the full cohomology groups, and introduces the neighbourhoods F^n of the limit topology.

Use the sharpened hypothesis (proof lines 4976-4990): for an element of F^n the author uses the chain condition on the graded module of stable images to find finitely many elements controlling it, which is where the stable images enter the argument.

Conclude the equality of topologies (proof lines 4990-5002): the containment I^n M contained in F^n and the reverse containment obtained from the finite control give that the limit topology is the I-adic topology.
proof_roadmap: Follow the companion argument with the stable images N_n replacing the full cohomology groups.
Use the ascending chain condition on the graded module of stable images to control elements of the neighbourhoods.
Conclude that the two topologies coincide.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the sharpened version of the comparison between the limit topology and the I-adic topology on M = lim H^p(C, F_n), with the ascending chain condition now imposed on the graded module of the stable images N_n (statement lines 4940-4961). The proof follows the companion argument of the same chapter, and its own content is the use of the sharpened hypothesis to control an element of the neighbourhoods through finitely many stable images (proof lines 4963-5002). The non-formal content is the substitution of the stable images for the full cohomology groups. The claim is H2: a variant whose proof is the companion proof with one ingredient sharpened.
